attacks.unsupported_mechanism: KILLED - claimed hydroxyl-radical oxidative kill of organisms during a 0.4 s dwell at specific energy 8 Wh/m3 (= ~28.8 kJ/m3, ~0.029 J/mL) cannot deliver the 3.5-log disinfection typically achieved by advanced-oxidation; cavitation-driven •OH chemistry reported in the literature requires tens of kJ/L (orders of magnitude higher) to generate sufficient radical flux for microbial inactivation, so the causal chain is physically invalid.
attacks.weak_transfer: KILLED - bench loop testable prediction at 5 m3/h cannot transfer to the 350 m3/h full-scale unit: cavitation number scales with rotor tip speed and geometry, and at 70x flow rate with the same 45 kW envelope the specific energy collapses by ~70x to ~0.11 Wh/m3, so the 8 Wh/m3 radical-yielding regime claimed on bench cannot be reproduced at full scale.
attacks.engineering_infeasibility: KILLED - 45 kW motor driving a rotor-stator at 350 m3/h cannot maintain cavitation number in the transient (inertial) cavitation regime required for radical generation while also handling the 80 NTU turbidity upper bound; rotor-stator erosion/clearance growth in sandy water is acknowledged, and at 80 NTU the erosion rate would destroy the clearances needed to sustain cavitation within a single ballast event.
attacks.regulatory_incompatibility: KILLED - IMO D-2 Ballast Water Management Convention requires the Biological Efficacy Standard to be demonstrated across the full operating envelope (including the stated 2-30 C, 8-36 PSU, and up to 80 NTU), and a single-pass device with collapsing cavitation at part-flow and no holding tank cannot reliably meet the D-2 organism discharge limits at the turbidity and temperature extremes named in the constraint set.
